sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Le Mans sets low, simple tariffs and restricts cars strictly in its old town. The city's parking page, last edited in June 2025, gives the street post-parking charge as 30 euros, 20 euros if paid within three days and 80 euros if nothing is paid within three months [2]. On-street parking is paid 9am to 12:30pm and 2pm to 7pm Monday to Saturday and is free on Sundays and public holidays [3]. Car traffic is regulated in the Cité Plantagenêt and on the central pedestrian plateau, with only residents and authorised users allowed in; the central area has badges, a maximum of two per household, and delivery tickets for up to 30 minutes between 5am and 11am [7]. In November 2025 ICI Maine reported a poster campaign, backed by the operator, for existing offers such as free first minutes in the car parks, a 'shopping + evening' offer from 3pm and 1 euro from 7pm to 7am; a municipal councillor said Le Mans is the cheapest city in western France for centre parking [6]. We found no official information on a low-emission zone.

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The largest change is the bus and tram programme. The Chronolignes programme rebuilds the three busiest bus lines, C4, C5 and C6, with 13 km of dedicated lanes still to be created, and turns Boulevard Nicolas-Cugnot from a ring road into an urban boulevard; all are plans [12]. The first lengthened tram unit entered service on 10 June 2026, ahead of the 24 Heures du Mans, raising capacity per unit from 211 to 296 passengers, with the other 33 to be extended by end 2027 [13]. Two park-and-ride sites serve the tram, Antarès and Université-Bartholdi, and a season ticket includes parking in them [11]. The Arsenal-Marais redevelopment, signed on 23 September 2026, plans over 700 homes and a multi-storey car park on former military land, with first demolitions in 2028, a long-term project [15]. The Halles car park was announced to close from 16 July to 20 September 2026 for works, with reopening planned for 21 September; on 21 October 2026 it was still shown as closed [17]. Cénovia lists 14 EV charge points in its centre car parks [9], and the metropolis has about 400 charge points against an estimated need of 2,000 in 2035 [10]. For the 24 Heures, the organiser recommends the tram and park-and-ride sites at motorway exits; details for the next edition were not yet published [14].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Cénovia Park, which the city entrusted with its underground car parks and paid street parking, describes itself as the parking operator of the conurbation, with about 6,100 car-park spaces in 16 public car parks and 173 on-street ticket machines [0]. The city's page lists, for example, République 774 spaces, Jacobins 388, Quinconces 610 underground plus 350 surface, Médiathèque 240 and Gare-Sud 269 [1]. At République, Jacobins and Quinconces P1 the first 15 minutes are free, 30 minutes cost 1 euro and four hours 7.50 euros; Quinconces P2 gives the first hour free [4]. The station car parks are priced steeply for short stays, except Gare Sud P2, at 1.50 euros an hour [5]. Cénovia launched Le Mans Parkings Partagés in 2024 for renting private spaces [8].

Our data cover 11 car parks with 3,286 spaces, measured since 5 October 2026. Occupancy averaged about 40% on weekdays and 36% at weekends, weighted by spaces. The Médiathèque is the fullest, at 76% on weekdays and 79% at weekends (240 spaces), followed by Rabelais (71%) and République (52% on weekdays, 33% at weekends). A twelfth feed, the hospital car park P3 (811 spaces), reads about 85% to 86% at every hour of the week, which we treat as a stuck counter and leave out. The Médiathèque is where Halles subscribers were redirected during the Halles closure [17], which may explain part of its load. The Gare Sud underground car park is a commuter facility, 51% on weekdays against 17% at weekends, while the two Quinconces car parks fill at weekends, 32% and 37% against 19% and 25% on weekdays. About two and a half weeks of data.
